questions.statement: Complete: "He ________ breakfast at 6:00 AM every morning."

options.feedback: Incorrect. For "he", the irregular form of "have" is "has".

questions.statement: "I ________ go to the gym on Mondays and Wednesdays." (Two days a week)

options.feedback: Incorrect. Always means 7 days a week.
Correct! Twice a week fits the "sometimes" or "often" frequency better than extremes.
Incorrect. "Never" means zero days.
Incorrect. "Twice" is not a frequency adverb used in this position before the verb without "a week".

questions.explanation:
The student understands the relative frequency described and chooses the best adverb.

questions.context:
A description of a friend's physical appearance.
"My best friend is Lucas. He has curly brown hair and he wears glasses. He is very tall."

options.text: He has straight hair and he is tall.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says his hair is curly.

options.text: He is short and wears glasses.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says he is tall.

options.text: He is tall and has curly hair.
options.feedback: Correct! These two features are explicitly mentioned.

options.text: He has brown eyes and glasses.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The eyes are not mentioned, only the hair.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading comprehension to verify physical description details.

questions.context: Analyzing negative structures in Present Simple vs Continuous.

questions.context:
Analyzing a person's routine and frequency.
"Julian is a student. He always goes to school in the morning. He never eats fast food. He usually plays soccer after class, but today he is studying at home for a test."

options.feedback: Incorrect. He "usually" plays soccer, but not today.
Incorrect. He "never" eats it.
Correct! The text explicitly mentions his action for today.
Incorrect. He is at home studying.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the contrast between a routine ("usually") and a current exception ("today") using different tenses.

questions.statement: What can we conclude about Clara's personality and goals?
questions.context:
Evaluating a student's introduction and intentions.
"Hello everyone! My name is Clara. I'm from Cali, the city of salsa. I'm 13 and I'm very excited to be here. I love music and I always practice the guitar after school. I want to be a famous musician one day."

options.text: She is a lazy person who only likes salsa.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She "always practices", which shows discipline.

options.text: She is a student from Bogotá who wants to play guitar.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She is from Cali.

options.text: She is a passionate and disciplined student with clear artistic goals.
options.feedback: Correct! Her love for music, daily practice, and ambition to be a musician support this.

options.text: She is a professional musician from Cali.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She is 13 and "wants to be" one day.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the description to infer character traits (passion, discipline) and confirm facts (origin, age, goals).
